headline: Callums Cape Storm Peaks as Nevish Line Falls Quiet
war_summary: Three hours on, the storm has changed its ground. Callums Cape, seething at our last writing, now bears the war's fiercest labour: eleven flag exchanges inside two hours, the last timed at this filing, some two thousand casualties between the sides in that span, and hourly losses still climbing, with Naofa and Scouts Jest the storm centres and the cape's seven posts split four and three. Godcrofts, silent through the day, has flared without warning, seven flag moves in the same short span, every one at Isawa. Mooring County's flags stir again about The Wind Hills after an evening's stillness, and Linn Mercy's fires, lately banked, have rekindled round Outwich Ranch. The Weathered Expanse remains restless, its two ruined works still unreclaimed. By contrast the Nevish Line, which led our previous edition, has logged no flag change since that morning report, though its daily toll tops sixteen thousand. Marban Hollow is still, and Callahans Passage, flag-silent since late evening, nonetheless shows casualty rates climbing. It is the seven hundred and eighty-fourth day of the war; thirty-four victory towns must fall, and no victor is declared.
